..
A minor, relatively dry trade-wind surge continues across the region.
The Guam and Saipan ASOS have reported sustained winds just below 20
knots, with Guam reporting isolated gusts up to 25 knots. On Thursday
night into Friday, model guidance indicates a trade-wind trough 
passing south of the region, bringing scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms, mainly concentrated over Guam. This was reflected in 
the forecast with a slight difference in shower chances between Guam 
and CNMI. Thunderstorm chances are more likely for Guam than the 
CNMI, but still included the latter in the forecast due to omega 
values and increased relative humidity in the Saipan model time 
heights. Gusts near heavier showers will be around 25 mph.
Considering ongoing drought concerns, conserving any upcoming 
rainfall should be a priority as the dry season approaches. Once the 
trough passes around Friday night, isolated showers may return for 
the rest of the forecast period.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are comprised of a dominant trade swell.
Moderate to fresh trade winds will persist throughout the forecast
period, possibly with isolated gusts up to 25 knots at times. 
Altimetry and model guidance suggests higher combined seas than 
previously anticipated as the trade swell continues to build, 
possibly reaching up to 7 feet over the weekend. This would produce 
surf capable of a high rip current risk along east-facing reefs, so 
those with marine interests should pay attention to the forecast over
the coming days.

Fire weather...
Although we are expecting a brief period of rainfall within the next
couple of days, it may not nearly be enough to delay the continued 
rise in the Keech-Bryam Drought Index (KBDI). Sustained trade winds
of 15 to 20 mph with gusts possibly up to 30 mph in higher elevations
will prevail, further increasing the potential for critical fire
weather conditions. Folks are urged to monitor any outdoor-
related activities that involve a spark or flames, as elevated 
conditions are ongoing.

Eastern Micronesia...
The main weather feature affecting Eastern Micronesia at this time is
a Near-Equatorial Trough (NET). This trough emerges from the 
southern hemisphere south of Chuuk and re-enters the southern 
hemisphere south of Majuro. Pohnpei is west of the main action, at 
least for now, and should be all night. That could even be true 
Thursday, but the activity to their east will likely be approaching 
them. Kosrae and Majuro are going to be in it for a while.

All in all, Pohnpei should have scattered showers from Thursday until
Sunday. Kosrae should have scattered showers from tonight through
Monday, or the entire forecast period. Majuro should have scattered
showers from tonight through Friday night, and on Monday as a new
system enters from across the date line. With the ongoing likelihood
of worsening drought conditions, any reasonable effort should be made
to collect any rainfall which is available.

Swell could be reaching, or would only be 1 foot below, high surf
advisory criteria at both Pohnpei and Kosrae Friday night through
Monday. Therefore, have headlines for elevated surf in these zones.
Majuro was getting close to having a headline for Monday, but fell
maybe about a foot short. There were two reasons they fell short, the
first was straight east swell, so no north facing reefs, and the
second was, the 12 foot criteria that Majuro has along east facing
reefs. However, if those wave heights hold, we might need a Small
Craft Advisory when the time gets closer.

Western Micronesia...
The NET remains the main weather maker in the region. The NET will 
produce an unsettled weather pattern through the beginning of next 
week, for Palau and Chuuk. Model guidance suggests daily rainfall 
totals of up to an inch through Monday. Overall, a wet rest of the 
week and beginning of next week is in store.

The NET will produce near breezy conditions for Yap for the next few
days. Trade winds of 15 to 20 mph (10 to 15 kt) with occasional 
gusts to 30 mph (25 kt) are to be expected. Model guidance suggests 
the NET will produce high-end scattered showers this weekend before 
drying back out for the beginning of next week.

This would be a great opportunity to catch rain and top off water 
reserves for all three locations. 

Combined seas of 5 to 7 feet are seen across the region. Seas are 
forecast to maintain the 5 to 7 foot range through the week. This 
will keep surf around 7 to 8 feet along north- and east-facing 
reefs. Seas and surf are expected to remain below advisory thresholds
of 10 foot seas and 9 foot surf. Light to moderate winds are 
expected throughout the region with occasional gusts to strong near 
Yap over the next few days. Winds will gradually taper down for the 
beginning of next week.
